body.statement: Suppose \(\Sigma^{SS}\succ0\) and \(\Sigma^{aa}\succ0\) for every \(a\in M\). Under the centered Gaussian law and the calibration and marginal sampling conditions, whenever \(\eta_{S,n}<1\) and every \(\eta_{a,n}<1\), the explicit radii in \(\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\) satisfy \(\Pr\{\mathcal O_S\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\}\ge1-\alpha\), and on this event \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)\). More explicitly, for any positive-definite \(\mathcal O'_S\) with \(u=d_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathcal O_S,\mathcal O'_S)\le\min\{\lambda_*/2,L_B^{-1}\}\), every order and observed view pair obey \(\|B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O'_S)-B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O_S)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_Bu\) and \(\|R_\pi^{ab}(\mathcal O'_S)-R_\pi^{ab}(\mathcal O_S)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u)=L_Ru\); every corresponding directed-path product changes by at most \(\omega_{\mathrm{path}}(u)=L_{\mathrm{path}}L_Bu\). Hence, if \(\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u)\le\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}/2\), then \(\Pi_S(\mathcal O'_S)\subseteq\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\). On the coverage event, if \(2\bar r_n(\alpha)\le\min\{\lambda_*/2,L_B^{-1}\}\), \(\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(2\bar r_n(\alpha))\le\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}/2\), and \(\omega_{\mathrm{path}}(2\bar r_n(\alpha))\le\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}/2\), then the Hausdorff distance induced by \(d_{\mathrm{coef}}\) from \(\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)\) to \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\) is at most \(2L_B\bar r_n(\alpha)\), and \(\widehat\prec_{S,n}(\alpha)=\prec_S\). Consequently, if \(\min(n_S,\min_{a\in M}n_a)\to\infty\), the two novel margins are bounded below by \(\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}>0\) and \(\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}>0\), and \(\alpha_n\to0\) with vanishing radii, then Hausdorff consistency and exact essential-poset recovery hold in probability.
body.justification: Set inversion makes uncertainty honest when the population output is non-singleton, while the explicit moduli translate covariance error into branch and ancestral-path stability.
body.gap: ChernozhukovHongTamer2007SetInference gives general contour inversion, while GhoshalHonorio2018LinearSEM uses precision-diagonal and nonzero-precision-entry gaps for one recursive graph. Neither source defines the wrong-order residual or common-ancestral path-product margins, nor derives the displayed LiMVAM covariance-to-margin moduli.
body.consumer: A future Cam-CAN MEG or fMRI diagnostic analysis can report an uncertainty-aware sensitivity envelope only after checking common-target sampling and failing to reject the component-aligned repeated-sensor mechanism on observed calibration blocks.
body.proof_tex:
Set \(K=K_{\mathrm{obs}}=m+1\) and
\[
t_\alpha=\sqrt{2\log(2K/\alpha)}.
\tag{1}
\]
We first prove simultaneous coverage. Consider one of the \(K\) covariance sources: either the aligned \(S\)-vector, with \((d,n,\Sigma_0)=(d_S,n_S,\Sigma^{SS})\), or the observations from view \(a\), with \((d,n,\Sigma_0)=(p,n_a,\Sigma^{aa})\). The selected case satisfies \(\Sigma_0\succ0\) by \(\text{ass:selected-joint-nondegeneracy}\). In every marginal case, \(\lambda_*>0\) and the definition of \(\lambda_*\) in \(\text{def:local-stability-modulus}\) give
\[
\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma^{aa})\ge\lambda_*>0,
\tag{2}
\]
so \(\Sigma_0\succ0\) there as well. Let \(Y\) be the \(n\times d\) data matrix whose rows are the sampled vectors transposed, and define
\[
G=Y\Sigma_0^{-1/2}.
\tag{3}
\]
The inverse square root in (3) exists in the selected case precisely because of \(\text{ass:selected-joint-nondegeneracy}\), and in the marginal cases by (2). By \(\text{ass:centered-gaussian-law}\), each row of \(G\) is centered Gaussian with identity covariance, hence has independent standard normal coordinates. By \(\text{ass:calibration-sampling}\) for the selected source and \(\text{ass:marginal-sampling}\) for a marginal source, the rows are independent and identically distributed. Thus all entries of \(G\) are independent standard normal variables.

For this source put
\[
\eta=\sqrt{d/n}+t_\alpha/\sqrt n.
\tag{4}
\]
The assumed inequality \(\eta<1\) implies \(n>d\), and in particular \(n\ge d\), so \(\text{lem:gaussian-extreme-singular-values}\) applies with \(t=t_\alpha\). Since \(2\exp(-t_\alpha^2/2)=\alpha/K\), with probability at least \(1-\alpha/K\),
\[
1-\eta\le s_{\min}(G)/\sqrt n
\le s_{\max}(G)/\sqrt n\le1+\eta.
\tag{5}
\]
Set \(\ell=(1-\eta)^2\) and \(v=(1+\eta)^2\). The empirical covariance is
\[
\widehat\Sigma
=\frac1nY^{\mathsf T}Y
=\Sigma_0^{1/2}\frac{G^{\mathsf T}G}{n}\Sigma_0^{1/2}.
\tag{6}
\]
Squaring (5) and applying the congruence in (6) yields
\[
\ell\Sigma_0\preceq\widehat\Sigma\preceq v\Sigma_0.
\tag{7}
\]
Because \(\eta<1\), \(\ell>0\). Hence (7) implies
\[
\Sigma_0\preceq\ell^{-1}\widehat\Sigma,
\qquad
\Sigma_0\succeq v^{-1}\widehat\Sigma.
\tag{8}
\]
If \(c=\ell^{-1}-1\), then \(1-v^{-1}\le c\), and (8) gives
\[
-c\widehat\Sigma
\preceq \Sigma_0-\widehat\Sigma
\preceq c\widehat\Sigma.
\tag{9}
\]
Taking Rayleigh quotients in (9) proves
\[
\|\Sigma_0-\widehat\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\bigl((1-\eta)^{-2}-1\bigr)
\|\widehat\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{10}
\]

For the selected source, (4) and (10) are exactly the radius \(r_{S,n}(\alpha)\); for view \(a\), they are exactly \(r_{a,n}(\alpha)\), by \(\text{def:covariance-region}\). A union bound over the \(K=m+1\) sources gives a joint event \(\mathcal E_n(\alpha)\) satisfying
\[
\Pr\{\mathcal E_n(\alpha)\}\ge1-K(\alpha/K)=1-\alpha.
\tag{11}
\]
No independence among the \(K\) covariance estimators is used in (11). On \(\mathcal E_n(\alpha)\), all inequalities defining \(\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\) hold for \(\mathcal O_S\). Its selected joint covariance is positive definite by \(\text{ass:selected-joint-nondegeneracy}\), and all its marginal covariances are positive definite by (2). Therefore
\[
\mathcal O_S\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\Pr\{\mathcal O_S\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\}\ge1-\alpha.
\tag{12}
\]
By the union in \(\text{def:region-inversion}\), (12) also gives
\[
\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)
\subseteq\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)
\quad\text{on }\mathcal E_n(\alpha).
\tag{13}
\]

We next establish the deterministic perturbation bounds. Fix a positive-definite \(\mathcal O'_S\), put
\[
u=d_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathcal O_S,\mathcal O'_S)
\le\min\{\lambda_*/2,L_B^{-1}\},
\tag{14}
\]
and fix an order \(\pi\), a view \(a\), a row label \(j\), and its predecessor set \(P\) under \(\pi\). The row is zero when \(P=\varnothing\), so suppose \(P\ne\varnothing\). In the notation of \(\text{def:modified-cholesky}\), write
\[
\beta=\Sigma^{aa}[j,P]\Sigma^{aa}[P,P]^{-1},
\qquad
\beta'=\Sigma'^{aa}[j,P]\Sigma'^{aa}[P,P]^{-1}.
\tag{15}
\]
Compression by coordinate-selection matrices does not increase operator norm. Consequently every covariance block in (15) changes by at most \(u\). For every unit vector \(x\), (2) and (14) imply
\[
x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma'^{aa}[P,P]x
\ge x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{aa}[P,P]x-u
\ge\lambda_*-u
\ge\lambda_*/2.
\tag{16}
\]
Thus
\[
\|\Sigma'^{aa}[P,P]^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2/\lambda_*.
\tag{17}
\]
The resolvent identity and (17) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\|\Sigma'^{aa}[P,P]^{-1}-\Sigma^{aa}[P,P]^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\\
&\qquad\le
\|\Sigma'^{aa}[P,P]^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\|\Sigma'^{aa}[P,P]-\Sigma^{aa}[P,P]\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\|\Sigma^{aa}[P,P]^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\frac{2u}{\lambda_*^2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
\]
Since \(\|\Sigma^{aa}[j,P]\|_2\le\|\Sigma^{aa}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le K_*\), subtracting (15), adding and subtracting \(\Sigma^{aa}[j,P]\Sigma'^{aa}[P,P]^{-1}\), and using (17)--(18) yields
\[
\|\beta'-\beta\|_2
\le\frac{2u}{\lambda_*}+\frac{2K_*u}{\lambda_*^2}
=2u(\lambda_*^{-1}+K_*\lambda_*^{-2}).
\tag{19}
\]
There are at most \(p\) rows. The operator norm is bounded by the Frobenius norm, so (19) and the definition of \(L_B\) in \(\text{def:local-stability-modulus}\) imply
\[
\|B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O'_S)-B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O_S)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le L_Bu.
\tag{20}
\]

Moreover, (14), (16), and \(\|\Sigma'^{aa}[j,P]\|_2\le K_*+u\) give
\[
\|\beta'\|_2
\le\frac{2(K_*+u)}{\lambda_*}
\le1+\frac{2K_*}{\lambda_*}.
\tag{21}
\]
The same upper bound also applies to \(\beta\). Hence, using \(L_\pi^{(a)}=I_p-B_\pi^{(a)}\), both the population and perturbed residualizers satisfy
\[
\|L_\pi^{(a)}\|_{\mathrm{op}},
\|L_\pi'{}^{(a)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le1+\sqrt p\left(1+\frac{2K_*}{\lambda_*}\right)
=G_*.
\tag{22}
\]
For an observed pair \((a,b)\), abbreviate the population residualizers by \(L_a,L_b\) and the perturbed residualizers by \(L'_a,L'_b\). From \(\text{def:residual-cross-blocks}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_\pi'{}^{ab}-R_\pi^{ab}
={}&L'_a(\Sigma'^{ab}-\Sigma^{ab})L_b'{}^{\mathsf T}
+(L'_a-L_a)\Sigma^{ab}L_b'{}^{\mathsf T}\\
&+L_a\Sigma^{ab}(L'_b-L_b)^{\mathsf T}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{23}
\]
By (20), (22), the definition of \(K_*\), and submultiplicativity,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|R_\pi'{}^{ab}-R_\pi^{ab}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
&\le\{G_*^2+2L_BG_*K_*\}u\\
&\le\{G_*^2+L_BG_*(2K_*+\lambda_*/2)\}u\\
&=L_Ru=\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u).
\end{aligned}
\tag{24}
\]

For an ordered vertex pair \(e=(v,w)\), define
\[
w_e(T)=\max_{a\in M}|B_{wv}^{(a)}|.
\tag{25}
\]
Equation (20) implies \(|w_e(T')-w_e(T)|\le L_Bu\). Population weights are at most \(K_B\); by (14), perturbed weights are at most \(K_B+1\). If \(g=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\) is a directed path for the fixed order, then \(1\le\ell\le p-1\). A telescoping product expansion therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\left|
\prod_{h=1}^{\ell}w_{(v_{h-1},v_h)}(T')
-\prod_{h=1}^{\ell}w_{(v_{h-1},v_h)}(T)
\right|\\
&\qquad\le \ell(K_B+1)^{\ell-1}L_Bu
\le(p-1)(K_B+1)^{p-2}L_Bu\\
&\qquad=L_{\mathrm{path}}L_Bu
=\omega_{\mathrm{path}}(u).
\end{aligned}
\tag{26}
\]

Now suppose \(\pi\notin\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\). By \(\text{ass:feasibility-separation}\) and \(\text{def:feasibility-margin}\), some distinct \(a,b\in S\) and some off-diagonal coordinate of \(R_\pi^{ab}\) have absolute value at least \(\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}\). Each entrywise change is at most the operator-norm change in (24). Consequently, if \(\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u)\le\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}/2\), the same coordinate of \(R_\pi'{}^{ab}\) has absolute value at least \(\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}/2>0\). The compatibility definition then excludes \(\pi\) at \(\mathcal O'_S\). Since this applies to every population-incompatible order,
\[
\Pi_S(\mathcal O'_S)\subseteq\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S).
\tag{27}
\]

Return to the coverage event \(\mathcal E_n(\alpha)\). If \(\mathcal O'_S\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\), then \(\mathcal O_S\) and \(\mathcal O'_S\) are each within the corresponding radius of the same empirical block. Every selected cross-block is a compression of the selected joint block. The triangle inequality and the definition of \(\bar r_n(\alpha)\) therefore yield
\[
d_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathcal O_S,\mathcal O'_S)
\le2\bar r_n(\alpha).
\tag{28}
\]
Assume the three small-radius inequalities displayed in the theorem. For every \(T'\in\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)\), \(\text{def:region-inversion}\) and \(\text{def:identified-tuple-set}\) provide \(\mathcal O'_S\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\) and \(\pi\in\Pi_S(\mathcal O'_S)\) such that
\[
T'=T_\pi(\mathcal O'_S).
\tag{29}
\]
Equations (27)--(28) give \(\pi\in\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\), while (20) gives
\[
d_{\mathrm{coef}}\bigl(T',T_\pi(\mathcal O_S)\bigr)
\le2L_B\bar r_n(\alpha).
\tag{30}
\]
Conversely, (13) puts every element of \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\) in \(\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)\). Thus both directed Hausdorff distances are controlled, and
\[
d_{\mathrm H}^{d_{\mathrm{coef}}}
\bigl(\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha),\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\bigr)
\le2L_B\bar r_n(\alpha).
\tag{31}
\]

It remains to identify the essential relation. Inclusion (13) immediately gives
\[
\widehat\prec_{S,n}(\alpha)\subseteq\prec_S,
\tag{32}
\]
because a relation common to the larger estimated tuple set is common to its population subset. Conversely, fix \(i\prec_S j\) and any \(T'\) as in (29). Its counterpart \(T=T_\pi(\mathcal O_S)\) belongs to \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\) by (27). By \(\text{ass:path-product-separation}\) and \(\text{def:path-margin}\), an \(i\)-to-\(j\) path in \(G_T\) has weight product at least \(\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}\). Equation (26) and the third small-radius inequality leave the same path product in \(T'\) at least \(\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}/2>0\). Every factor is therefore positive, so every edge of that path occurs in the union support graph \(G_{T'}\). Thus \(i\widehat\prec_{S,n}(\alpha)j\). Combined with (32) and \(\text{def:essential-poset}\), this proves
\[
\widehat\prec_{S,n}(\alpha)=\prec_S.
\tag{33}
\]

Finally take \(\alpha=\alpha_n\). By the stated vanishing-radii condition, \(\bar r_n(\alpha_n)\to0\) in probability and the radii are eventually defined with probability tending to one. Since \(\lambda_*,L_B,L_R,L_{\mathrm{path}},\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}},\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}\) are fixed positive population quantities, the three small-radius inequalities hold on an event \(\mathcal H_n\) with \(\Pr(\mathcal H_n)\to1\). Equation (11) and \(\alpha_n\to0\) give
\[
\Pr\{\mathcal E_n(\alpha_n)\cap\mathcal H_n\}
\ge1-\alpha_n-\Pr(\mathcal H_n^{\mathsf c})\longrightarrow1.
\tag{34}
\]
On this intersection, (31) is bounded by \(2L_B\bar r_n(\alpha_n)=o_P(1)\), and (33) holds exactly. Therefore the coefficient sets converge in Hausdorff distance in probability and the essential poset is recovered exactly with probability tending to one.
